Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, I pulled together a concise mutual action plan (MAP) focused on two items you flagged: capacity reservation lead times for Dedicated/Private deployments and initial GPU pool sizing for your fraud-detection inference workload. The attached PDF is the MAP; the spreadsheet contains the sizing assumptions we discussed.

High level summary:
- Recommended starting pool: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (p100-equivalent if you have strict budget constraints) to support ~250 qps peak with 75ms P95 token latency under your 1.2k token average sequences.
- Private/VPC lead time: 8–10 weeks for full on-prem provisioning (OS/hardware procurement + HSM/KMS integration).
- Dedicated lead time: 3–5 weeks to reserve and configure a dedicated GPU pool in our cloud regions (shorter if we match an existing instance type).

Open items we need to close:
1) Finalize target P95 latency and peak concurrent sessions (you mentioned 200–300).
2) Confirm whether caching/prefix reuse from historical traffic is acceptable (saves ~20–30% GPU).
3) Procurement timeline/PO owner at FinTechCorp so we can lock capacity.

Next steps I propose:
- You + procurement confirm PO target date by Friday, Mar 12.
- Dev (cc’d) will send a short technical addendum with exact CPU/RAM and network requirements for the on-prem option by Monday.
- I’ll schedule a 30-minute MAP review with your infra and security teams next week to align on SOC2/Evidence we need for Private.

I attached a first-pass MAP and a capacity estimate workbook — happy to update after Dev’s sizing note. Looking forward to getting this into your roadmap.

Hi Samantha —

Quick technical addendum as requested (keeps to the facts so procurement/infra can slot into their processes):

Private (on-prem) provisioning lead time: 
- Typical vendor procurement + rack/cabling: 4–6 weeks (hardware lead times can vary by vendor).
- Redwood deployment + secure onboarding (KMS/HSM, network peering, audit logging): 2–4 weeks.
- Total observed range: 8–10 weeks. Variance drivers: custom hardware orders, HSM sourcing, local permitting for racks.

Dedicated (Redwood-managed) provisioning lead time: 
- Capacity reservation + configuration in our cloud region: 3–5 weeks.
- We can reduce to 1–2 weeks if you accept a different instance SKU but we will validate P95 latency first.

GPU pool sizing note (assumptions based on your payload):
- Baseline: 8x A100-equivalent (single-model serving) => supports ~250 qps with 75ms P95 token latency for 1.2k token sequences.
- With prefix/KV caching and batching tuned: effective capacity increases ~25% => 10–11x equivalent GPUs.
- Suggested redundancy/rolling upgrade buffer: +2 GPUs to maintain availability during upgrades (so plan for 10 GPUs target).

Rack/power/network for Private:
- Each A100-equivalent node: ~3U, 750–900W under load (sizing depends on power supply choice).
- For 10-node pool: estimate 30U and ~9kW peak; recommend N+1 PSU and 15–20kW PDUs for headroom and cooling.

Procurement risk if PO is delayed:
- Dedicated: delaying PO by >4 weeks increases time-to-production linearly with reservation slot availability. In practice, a missed PO window can push launch by 3–6 weeks if regional capacity is tight.
- Private: missed PO delays are magnified (hardware lead times compound). A 2–4 week delay in ordering can extend the end-to-end timeline by 4–8 weeks.

I attached a short XLS with per-node power/space numbers and cost delta profiles for A100 vs alternative SKUs. Happy to jump on a call to walk infra/procurement through this tomorrow.

—Dev
